notes: THE TAX CART (client/scenes/court/chests_view.gd), a Court view cut from chests.png in four bands laid edge to edge -- the header scene (THE TAX CART baked, its line lifted: the interval is the server's), the cart's big painting, the controls row (the stock panel emptied of its carts, the hourglass panel with its empty plate; OPEN and the (i) lifted and cut as their own buttons), the three cards of a cart's round (in the yard, on the road, opened) with their empty caption plates -- and the foot's foliage, pinned to the screen's foot.

The painting sits 16 units lower than the chrome: its pills are at y 37..96, the chrome's at 21..79. So every band but the foot is drawn 16 higher than it was painted (the header is cut from y 16), which puts the painted pills exactly under the chrome's and leaves only their ends and lower rims to repair. The foot is drawn where it was painted, from y 1499, its top 16 rows (the plates' lower rims) replaced by the foliage under them mirrored up.

Under the pills and the painted COURT plate: each is lifted whole (the chrome's pill corners are cut, and would show a painted pill through them), the parts left in view -- the rims under the chrome's pills, the gold pill's ends, the plate's right end and its lower rows below CourtBack's plate -- are the painting beside them mirrored over (patch), and only what the chrome covers is left to Telea.

crops.name: chests/header
crops.note: The scene under the pills, from y 16 (drawn at 0). THE TAX CART is baked (fixed copy). Its line -- 'The crown's cart returns every four hours.', ivory ink x 181..691, caps 295..315, the y's tail to 325 -- is lifted by its ink and set live from the cart's interval. Pills: gold x 171..407, diamonds 427..643, energy 665..908, y 37..96; the COURT plate x 171..362, y 128..185 (CourtBack's covers x 165..327, y 122..171 in the painting's units).

crops.name: chests/scene
crops.note: The cart before the gate in its gilt frame (outer rim x 162..927, y 407..1045), with the navy either side. Drawn at y 388.

crops.name: chests/controls
crops.note: The controls row on its navy, drawn at y 1030: the silver stock panel (rim x 164..402, y 1066..1161) with its three painted carts lifted row by row from its own clean columns either side -- the view draws one per place, lit or grey -- and the hourglass panel (rim x 412..636; its empty plate x 493..622, y 1085..1140, where the time to the next cart is set). OPEN and the (i) are lifted to the ground (x 648..923) and drawn as their own buttons, so a dimmed OPEN shows no painted corner round it.

crops.name: chests/cart_lit
crops.note: The first painted cart, gold and lit (ink x 187..242, y 1094..1138), its glow kept: a cart waiting in the yard.

crops.name: chests/cart_dim
crops.note: The third painted cart, grey iron (ink x 330..382, y 1095..1134): a place in the yard with no cart in it.

crops.name: chests/open
crops.note: OPEN, word and all (outer rim x 648..846, y 1066..1159, corners cut 11).

crops.name: chests/info
crops.note: The gold (i) coin (ink x 855..923, y 1075..1142): the published odds. Its face is held solid, the rim's dark shading within the key of the navy.

crops.name: chests/cards
crops.note: The three cards of a cart's round on their navy, drawn at y 1161: in the yard (frame x 165..408), on the road (419..654), opened (664..923), frames y 1179..1466, each with its empty caption plate (x 170..402, 425..650, 672..917; y 1465..1513) where the view sets its line. The painting's lit COURT entry points its gold arrow into the gutter (x 142..166, y 1387..1425): the gutter and the first card's rim are carried down over it from the rows above, since the shell draws its own arrow where its rail puts COURT.

crops.name: chests/card_opened
crops.note: The third card alone, the chest opened on the cart, with its plate (the plate's chamfered foot kept, the ground beside it cut away): the opening's ceremony shows it with the prize's name in the plate.

crops.name: chests/footer
crops.note: The foliage and the wall under the cards, pinned to the screen's foot. Its top 16 rows held the plates' lower rims; they are the foliage below mirrored up, so the foot reaches the cards (drawn 16 higher) with nothing of the plates in it.
